palette.notes: Wiki: 54-colour master palette; each 8x8/8x16 sprite gets 3 colours + transparent; max 25 on screen (13 bg + 12 sprite). Clips: flat grey stone, brown wood, one saturated hero colour (green tunic, red-blue suit).

lighting: No real light: flat fills with one shade step; form comes from a dark outline and a single darker colour, not from a light source. Background bricks are one value darker than the floor.
silhouette: Tiny chibi sprites with big heads, thick dark outline and one dominant costume colour, so the hero reads at 1x against a grey wall; HUD (hearts, item icons) sits in a hard band on top.

motion.timing: Few frames, held long: walk cycles are 2-3 poses, the guard swaps one pose per beat; the Spider-Man clip is a 3-shot loop (perch, web-swing, leap) repeating about every 7.5 s.

texture: Tiled 8x8/16x16 brick and window patterns, no gradients; any shading is a flat second colour or dither. Attribute blocks (16x16 per subpalette) force colours to change only on tile edges.
camera: Locked side-on screen, no zoom; scene changes are hard cuts between fixed screens (rooftop, wall, sky). The explainer clip punches in on sprites and a palette grid.

acting.enters: Hero walks in from the left edge toward an NPC; Spider-Man appears perched, already in pose.
acting.acts: Zelda-style gag: hero walks up, a 'Speak' prompt appears, guard blocks with his axe, hero backs off and tries again; each try is a short beat.
acting.exits: Hero retreats to the left side of the frame rather than leaving it; the loop resets with a cut.
acting.depth: None: everything sits on one floor line; scale never changes. Depth is faked only by background bricks behind a wooden frame.

techniques: 3 colours + transparent per sprite: one dark outline, one base, one highlight
dark outline around the whole sprite so it reads on a busy tiled wall
tiled backgrounds on a 16x16 grid with colour changes only on tile edges
2-3 frame walk cycles held long, pose-to-pose
repeat-the-attempt gag: same approach, same refusal, small variation each time
HUD band as a framing device for the scene
feel: flat grey tiles + one saturated chibi hero + 3-colour sprites + repeat-the-attempt loop = readable retro comedy
for_fred: Use the repeat-the-attempt gag: Fred swims up to Pixie (or a button), gets refused, backs off to the edge, tries again with a small change, and on the third try something different happens. Keep Fred to 3-4 colours with a dark outline so he reads at 1x on a busy background.
